sources.title: Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," says lead dev
sources.text: The Helix is reportedly expected to launch in 2028 Jason Ronald – vice president of Xbox's gaming devices and ecosystem team – has spoken in more detail about what Project Helix actually is. Namely, it doesn't sound like it's a Steam Machine. To celebrate the 25th anniversary since the original Xbox was released and Halo arrived in our lives (and almost 26 since The Rock revealed the console ), Microsoft has released a magazine about the platform online . While a lot of it is about the history of the console, some details about the future of Xbox are sprinkled in there, with news about future releases like Fable, and a hint that there's maybe something going on with games like Crash Bandicoot and Tony Hawk. But the most significant bit of info is some more details about what Project Helix is. Ronald – who Microsoft describes as the vice president of next generation – says "it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," while touting its backwards compatibility capabilities, mentioning that he's "able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly." He also speaks about removing "the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games," while explaining more about what Project Helix's rumored PC connection actually is. "We're very clear on the design goal" Ronald explains, "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games." Of course, the real question is how all-encompassing is the PC integration going to be. Presumably the Xbox Store is a sure bet, and probably Battle.net too. But the idea of having your Steam library available on console would be a pretty unassailable win for the console, but sadly I really don't see that happening in the age of Steam Machines. Xbox Project Helix console could cost as much as $1,800 and is reportedly set to launch by Christmas 2028. sources.title: Microsoft Says Of The Next Xbox: ‘Helix Is A Console Capable Of Playing PC Games’
sources.text: Microsoft has put out an online magazine to celebrate 25 years of Xbox , and unquestionably to attempt even more damage control after a gruesome year of studio closures and mass layoffs. Within all the huff and puff lies a surprise: seven pages’ coverage of Project Helix, the codename for the next Xbox console. Within this is revealed the plan for Helix to be able to play games and even progress from every previous Xbox generation, as well as removing “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.” So, asks the magazine and indeed us, “is Project Helix a console or a PC?” The answer is very definitively: a console. Sort of. The current generation of consoles were notably described ahead of launch as being far more like PCs in a sealed box than the traditional console designs of yore, and this appears to be something Microsoft is looking to get away from this time out. The emphasis here is on the so-called instantaneous nature of a console. Jason Ronald is Xbox’s VP of “next generation,” and is quoted saying, “When I think about what makes a console magical, it’s that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don’t have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings.” Which is…a bold claim, given anyone who owns an Xbox will know about having to install the latest updates, waiting for game patches to excruciatingly slowly download without taking advantage of your 1TB ethernet connection, or that unbearable pause each time you load it up for it to fill in the dashboard. But of Project Helix, Ronald says, “it’s really designed to be the ultimate gaming machineâone that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I’m able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly,” adding, “We’re very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games.” However, it’s hard to know just how clear this distinction is from Ronald’s very next words. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.” So it is a PC then? So confused. Other comments from Ronald include that “We don’t think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metricsâit’s really about gameplay innovation.” He adds, “It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways.” Which all rather seems to be laying the ground for a machine that’s not focusing on the very latest and most expensive chipsets, but rather one that’ll take advantage of the more recent progress in upscaling and the like, perhaps to prevent the machine costing an absolute fortune? This topic isn’t ignored. Describing it as a factor “the team couldn’t have foreseen when Project Helix began,” the component crisis gets a mention. “Meeting this challenge has become a primary driver of Helix’s innovation,” says the article. Ronald is quoted once more. “It’s definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it’s also one of the most exciting times because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable.” This, he says, is why there’s the focus on neural rendering, adding, “I think you’re going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you’ve seen in the last 10 years.” It’s all a lot of words to avoid pointing out that Microsoft itself is one of the primary causes of the crisis in the first place, one arm taking all the available components from the other in order to power its AI hubris. Beyond this, the piece delivers some very confusing messaging regarding Xbox’s current desperate rebranding. After a disastrous attempt to call everything from your console to your toaster “an Xbox,” the recent emphasis has been to return to the core idea of the Xbox itself, yet that message gets very lost in Microsoft’s own marketing. We’re told at once that this is all about “the Return of Xboxâthe return of a console,” and then that “Project Helix aims to take a wrecking ball to the dividers currently keeping players and their games apart,” quoting Ronald saying Helix is about “enabling [players] to experience those games wherever they choose to play. It’s about removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past.” So which is it? There are claims the new UI will adapt to whether the Xbox is being played on the living room TV, or streamed to a mobile device or a PC with mouse and keyboard. This really does sound like a confusion of previous messaging crashing into the current reverse-ferret. There’s no word one when we can expect to see Project Helix in more detail, and certainly nothing on an intended release date. It seems that Microsoft and Sony are currently playing chicken on revealing whether they’re aiming for 2027 or 2028, or perhaps even later given the tumult in the hardware industry. But at least we know it’s a console, not a PC, but also like a PC, and can be streamed to your mobile, or played on PC, and has all of the annoying complexity of PCs taken away, but also still there. sources.text: Xbox is all-in on neural rendering to keep costs down A lead developer on Xbox Project Helix says that rising hardware costs are a primary driver of the upcoming console's development. As part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future . This online magazine includes an interview with Jason Ronald, vice president of next-generation console development at Microsoft and the lead for Project Helix. In this interview, he clarifies that Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," rather than the other way around. Obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost. Hardware prices are rising thanks to the ongoing global RAM shortages brought on by AI companies who just need to let your weird uncle generate what he looks like as a Simpson to post on Facebook. The Xbox Series X|S , PS5 , and Nintendo Switch 2 have all had price increases over the past year, but Ronald says keeping the price down is a crucial motivator in the console's design. "It's definitely a challenging time," Ronald says, adding, "it’s also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable." He explains the cost factor is why the team behind Project Helix is "really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it’s an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that." Obviously AI-assisted tech was a big talking point within games before the memory crisis, but it feels like it's only going to become more prominent. Sony has been implementing QSSR frame generation tech into its PS5 games , likely in part because nobody can afford a PS5 Pro now that it's almost $1,000. And with things going like they are, it's probably going to be the norm heading forward… let's just hope Xbox puts its money where its mouth is and actually makes the Helix affordable. But given the current rumor is it's going to be $1,800, I'm not too hopeful. sources.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
sources.text: "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering." Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable. The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday , and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games. "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation. "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering." While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future , saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future. The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld . "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players." Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

sources.title: Xbox afirma que Project Helix é um console capaz de rodar jogos de PC — e não o contrário
sources.text: A Microsoft divulgou novos detalhes sobre o Project Helix, seu console de nova geração, e reforçou a ideia de que o videogame é capaz de rodar jogos de PC — mas não um PC que consegue rodar jogos de console. Em entrevista publicada na revista especial de 25 anos do Xbox, Jason Ronald, vice-presidente da próxima geração da marca, explicou que o projeto foi desenvolvido para funcionar como um console tradicional, e não como um computador com recursos de videogame. “O Helix foi projetado para ser um console capaz também de rodar jogos do seu PC. Não é um PC que também roda jogos de console”, afirmou Ronald. O executivo também destacou que o aparelho pretende eliminar barreiras entre as bibliotecas de jogos de PC e Xbox, na intenção de manter a experiência simples e intuitiva para os jogadores. Segundo Ronald, a proposta do Project Helix é reunir diferentes bibliotecas em um único dispositivo e permitir com que os jogadores acessem seus títulos com mais facilidade. O console também deve oferecer compatibilidade com quatro gerações de jogos e preservar o progresso das contas Xbox. O executivo explicou que a experiência poderá ser adaptada a diferentes perfis de jogadores. Quem preferir uma experiência tradicional terá acesso rápido aos jogos, enquanto usuários mais avançados poderão personalizar configurações e opções de desempenho. “Quando penso no que torna um console mágico, é o fato de ele tornar meus jogos instantaneamente acessíveis e prontos para jogar”, afirmou Ronald. Ele também destacou que os jogadores não precisarão se preocupar com atualizações de drivers ou configurações típicas de um PC. A ideia, segundo o executivo, é criar uma plataforma que reúna a praticidade dos consoles com a flexibilidade dos computadores. “Quando pensamos no Project Helix, ele foi realmente concebido para ser a máquina de jogos definitiva — uma que remove todas as barreiras de jogo que existiram historicamente”, declarou. Durante a entrevista, Ronald também comentou sobre os desafios de desenvolver um novo console em meio à crise de componentes de PC. Segundo ele, a Microsoft está investindo em tecnologias como a renderização neural para melhorar o desempenho sem exigir mais poder computacional ou memória. “É definitivamente um momento desafiador, mas, como designer de sistemas e plataformas, também é um dos momentos mais empolgantes”, afirmou. O executivo explicou que a equipe busca novas soluções para avançar tecnologicamente e, ao mesmo tempo, manter os custos de produção e os preços sustentáveis. Ronald citou a renderização neural como uma das principais apostas para a próxima geração. A tecnologia pode abranger diferentes técnicas de processamento de imagem, como aprimoramento de resolução, geração de quadros e reconstrução de iluminação, embora a Microsoft ainda não tenha detalhado como pretende aplicá-la no Project Helix. O executivo também afirmou que a próxima geração não deve ser definida apenas por especificações tradicionais — como resolução 8K ou taxas de atualização de 240 Hz. Para ele, o foco estará em novas experiências de jogo, maior imersão e avanços visuais mais eficientes. E você, está ansioso para conhecer a próxima geração de consoles? stories.summary: We explore the inside jokes and little secrets tucked in every corner of the GTA maps.

sources.title: The History of Grand Theft Auto Easter Eggs
sources.text: When you’ve got an open world as big and dense as Grand Theft Auto, you’ve got to fill it with something. Restaurants, tennis courts, hidden packages, Strangers and Freaks. All kinds of treats to reward our exploration, some buried deeper than others. From hearts and minds to signs and shrines, the inside jokes and little secrets Rockstar’s calling card tucked in every corner of the map. This is the history of Grand Theft Auto easter eggs. The top-down Grand Theft Autos are too sparse and pixelated for the kind of buried treasures that would await us in the 3D era, but easter eggs exist even in this perspective. The most famous secret of the first GTA games involves lines of chanting bald NPCs dressed in orange robes, evocative of the Hare Krishna devotees famous for descending upon travelers at airports. If you can run the entire procession down sequentially, you’re rewarded with a seemingly nonsensical shout of “GOURANGA!” The phrase, a Krishna term meaning “be happy,” became the series’ signature meme among the early fanbase and resurfaced in the first few sequels, with hidden bonuses for mowing down Elvis impersonators in GTA 2 and football hooligans in GTA: London. For a series so devoted to examining the American dream, it’s easy to forget that Grand Theft Auto is British-born. The Scottish studio that created the series and the English brothers who made it a phenomenon belong to a storied Britdev tradition of taking the mick in the margins. From the ZX Spectrum emulator Rare buried in GoldenEye to Team17’s profane cheat codes and salty rants against Amiga Power magazine, British studios excel at hiding cheeky winks within their games. DMA Design, later Rockstar North, is no exception. DMA logos are disguised among the scenery, the pager randomly rags on staffers, and director Keith Hamilton himself sends you on a mission to find “the elements of GTA.” You can unlock R-rated language by naming your character after the studio’s credited “Project Bloke.” The developers are sharing their private jokes with the players, leaving their signatures in out-of-reach places. It’s been that way since the very first easter egg: The people in the game are talking to us, but they make it hard to hear them. The developers are very present in GTA 3. The game came in hot, suffered hurried changes, and still showed a lot of its arcadey roots. The veil between the game and its inner workings is thinnest here, you can out of bounds and fly the unflyable dodo across nonexistent towns named after team members. Look to La Luna through the eyes of a sniper rifle and pull the trigger to change the size of the moon, since the devs never decided how big it should be. You had to be willing to break the game a little bit to earn your peek behind the curtain, but it wasn’t that hard to do in 2001. Rockstar anticipated our escape. If you drive up a staircase near a parking lot in Staunton Island, you can hop out and use your car to climb onto a normally inaccessible roof. A precision jump drops you in an unused back alley, where you’ll find a sign that says “You weren’t supposed to be able to get here, you know.” The devs mercifully included a ramp to get us back into the game proper rather than risking a softlock. They knew we’d be snooping around. Some developers would dummy out this kind of content once it's discovered, but Rockstar maintained it as a running gag, slapping messages in hard-to-find spots throughout the series. In GTA: Vice City, Tommy can clip through a wall near the VCN helipad to enter a room with a simple marvel pedestal, upon which rests a single egg emblazoned “Happy Easter!” You’ll find no such ovoid in GTA: San Andreas. The closest you’ll come is the Gant Bridge that connects San Fierro with Las Venturas. The visitor center below contains a display serving up fun facts about the bridge. On closer inspection the text is actually information on the structure’s internal game files, like how it’s made up of 16,000 polygons and takes up a “staggering 1.27mb of disc space.” The sign was actually updated by Grove Street Games for the Definitive Edition release. After 17 years, the bridge’s triangle count doubled, the textures increased fourfold, and the disk space increased a whopping 3,000 percent. Good thing storage has stayed so affordable! If CJ can tear himself away from the field trip exhibits and land himself on top of the southern suspension tower, he’ll find another secret scolding among the orange steel rivets: “There are no Easter Eggs up here. Go away.” Clearly anticipating you’d be crushed by the disappointment of your futile search, Rockstar eases the pain with a handy parachute to get you back on your feet. Grand Theft Auto 4 does the bit, too. And cleverly, though nothing mind-blowing for the most part. A museum placard giving out about how hard the dinosaur skeletons were to sculpt, or a warning inside of the Statue of Happiness, through a door in the base reached only by air. “No hidden content,” reads an engraving by a collision-free closed door. Walk through the illusory wall, however and you’ll encounter something far more visceral than anything that’s come before. Inside you’ll find a ladder vanishing upwards into the body of the rusted copper colossus. Reach the top and you’ll find a scaffold standing just below a huge and hideous heart. Suspended painfully from chains, its maddening beat thunders inside the internal steel chamber and it cannot die. You’re not going to fit this thing in a bunny’s basket. It’s a darker, more unsettling easter egg than any that’s come before, even if it’s apparently just a jab at Hillary Clinton, who had gone after Rockstar hard as a senator during the San Andreas Hot Coffee scandal. The Heart of Liberty City is the stuff that creepypastas are made of, legends spread in schoolyards and over IRC. The series had outgrown this style of secret by the time of GTA 5. sources.title: GTA 6 streaming restrictions in China apparently don't allow any grand theft auto
sources.text: Or violence, or most forms of debauchery, really GTA 6 's apparent streaming rules in China effectively turn the game into a sightseeing simulator, and presumably severely restrict story playthroughs. Despite GTA 6 not actually releasing in mainland China – with many likely to import the game's Hong Kong release – Yahoo Taiwan reports (via machine translation) that Douyin (Mainland China and Hong Kong's version of TikTok) has acquired the rights to stream GTA 6 in China. This seems to have coincided with Rockstar opening a Douyin account to advertise pre-loading for the game on the platform. However, this was followed by TikTok reportedly releasing a series of guidelines for anyone keen to stream the game. While the guidelines were not released to the public, a TikTok creator has apparently revealed them by sharing a URL from a domain owned by Douyin and TikTok creator ByteDance. However, access to the document was reportedly disabled once reports about its content emerged. Obviously, GTA is known for its violence, drugs, sex, and all flavors of debauchery the player can partake in as part of its open world. But these supposed guidelines apparently prohibit players from livestreaming aspects of the game like stealing cars (grand theft auto, if you will), attacking civilians, using emojis, wearing revealing clothing, and fighting police officers. On top of that, it's requested that players black out the screen or adjust its color to avoid showing bloodshed. A reportedly leaked part of the document shows similar color-changing being used for Resident Evil Requiem . Obviously, this has been somewhat clowned on, as without all of that, what does GTA 6 have left? With people reportedly joking that it turns the game into a good morals simulator while questioning whether any of the story will even be playable under these restrictions, given that Lucia and Jason are seemingly in constant conflict with the police. That being said, Rockstar has said that GTA 6 will "provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy in the game, so perhaps it won't be too far off for some people's playthroughs. But hey, at least that version of the game will be welcome to some people . sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj released dozens of GTA 6 videos to the public more than a year before the game was formally revealed. The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. sources.text: GTA 6 ganha novo teaser e inicia preload após recorde de pré-vendas Arion Kurtaj, responsável pelo vazamento de quase 100 vídeos de GTA 6 em 2022 , se declarou culpado de todas as acusações relacionadas ao ataque contra os sistemas da Rockstar nesta segunda (16). O hacker, que tinha 17 anos na época, agora tem 21 e foi considerado apto a enfrentar um julgamento criminal no Reino Unido. Inicialmente, médicos haviam considerado Kurtaj inapto para participar de um julgamento tradicional e ele foi encaminhado a um hospital psiquiátrico de segurança máxima. Após uma nova avaliação, porém, o jovem foi transferido para uma prisão comum em janeiro e levado ao Tribunal da Coroa de Woolwich, onde admitiu os crimes — conforme relatado pelo BBC . Kurtaj fazia parte do grupo de hackers Lapsus$ quando invadiu os sistemas da Rockstar em 2022. Na época, ele divulgou quase 100 vídeos de gameplay e diversas capturas de tela de GTA 6 , que ainda estava em desenvolvimento e nem sequer havia recebido seu primeiro trailer oficial. O material revelou detalhes importantes sobre o jogo, incluindo a menção de uma protagonista feminina, posteriormente confirmada como Lucia. A quantidade de informações divulgadas foi tão grande que parte do público chegou a duvidar da autenticidade dos arquivos. Na época, médicos consideraram que Kurtaj não tinha condições de participar de um julgamento convencional devido à gravidade de seu autismo. Por isso, ele foi submetido a um chamado julgamento dos fatos, no qual o júri deveria avaliar se ele havia cometido os atos atribuídos a ele, sem determinar sua intenção criminosa. Em dezembro de 2023, o tribunal determinou que o hacker permanecesse internado em um hospital de segurança máxima por tempo indeterminado, a menos que médicos concluíssem que ele não representava mais um perigo. Uma avaliação posterior, realizada no fim do ano passado, considerou Kurtaj apto a responder criminalmente pelos crimes, mas ele acabou se declarando culpado de todas as acusações. O ataque à Rockstar aconteceu enquanto Kurtaj estava em liberdade sob fiança por outros crimes de hacking e recebia proteção policial. Ele estava hospedado em um hotel da rede Travelodge, em Bicester, após receber ameaças de hackers rivais relacionadas a bitcoins roubados. Como seu computador havia sido confiscado, Kurtaj utilizou um Amazon Fire Stick conectado à televisão do quarto, além de teclado e mouse Bluetooth, para acessar os sistemas internos da Rockstar. Com isso, conseguiu roubar dados da empresa, incluindo cerca de 90 vídeos que somavam quase uma hora de gameplay de GTA 6 . Depois da invasão, o hacker acessou o Slack interno da Rockstar e ameaçou divulgar o código-fonte do jogo caso a empresa não entrasse em contato com ele pelo Telegram em até 24 horas. Como a companhia não atendeu à exigência, ele publicou os arquivos em um fórum usando o nome de usuário TeaPotUberHacker . A Rockstar estimou que o ataque gerou US$ 5 milhões em custos de recuperação, além de milhares de horas de trabalho da equipe. A empresa também confirmou que o vazamento revelou antecipadamente a existência de uma protagonista feminina, informação que estava sendo mantida em sigilo para a campanha de divulgação do jogo. Arion Kurtaj não deve ser confundido com o CYBERLEEK , responsável por uma série de vazamentos de GTA 6 nos últimos meses . São episódios distintos, separados por anos e atribuídos a agentes diferentes — embora ambos envolvam informações internas do jogo da Rockstar. Os materiais atribuídos ao CYBERLEEK incluem imagens de gameplay e informações sobre sistemas que estariam presentes em GTA 6 . Entre os conteúdos divulgados estão detalhes sobre o mapa de Leonida, possíveis mecânicas de resistência e até um sistema de honra semelhante ao de Red Dead Redemption 2 . Também é importante considerar que as imagens parecem mostrar versões antigas de GTA 6 , possivelmente gravadas há mais de um ano. Portanto, recursos e mecânicas vistos nos vídeos podem ter sido modificados ou removidos pela Rockstar antes do lançamento. Após os vazamentos de 2022 e as novas divulgações atribuídas ao CYBERLEEK, GTA 6 está cada vez mais perto de chegar ao público. Ansioso para finalmente jogar o game na próxima quinta (19)? At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse. As the BBC reports , he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced. Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret. "We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way." Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up .

sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time de 1998 x remake de 2026: o que mudou em 28 anos?
sources.text: Lançado originalmente em 1998 para Nintendo 64 , The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time se tornou um dos jogos mais importantes da história dos videogames. Agora, 28 anos depois, o clássico retorna em uma versão completamente reconstruída para o Nintendo Switch 2 . O remake, lançado em 5 de novembro de 2026, preserva a essência da aventura de Link em Hyrule, mas incorpora recursos que não eram possíveis no hardware original. Entre as principais novidades estão os gráficos modernizados, cenas cinematográficas, atualizações no combate e, pela primeira vez na história da franquia, localização completa em português brasileiro, incluindo dublagem . Mas o que realmente mudou entre as duas versões? Uma das diferenças mais evidentes está na apresentação visual. Em 1998, Ocarina of Time representou um marco para os jogos tridimensionais. O Nintendo 64 permitiu que Link explorasse Hyrule em ambientes 3D, com movimentação livre, diferentes regiões e um sistema de câmera que ajudou a estabelecer padrões para os jogos de ação e aventura. Entretanto, as limitações tecnológicas da época eram evidentes nos modelos dos personagens, nas texturas e na complexidade dos cenários. O remake de 2026 apresenta uma reconstrução visual da aventura, com ambientes mais detalhados, personagens remodelados e cenas cinematográficas atualizadas. A proposta da Nintendo, segundo as avaliações da imprensa especializada, foi modernizar a apresentação sem descaracterizar a identidade visual e a atmosfera do jogo original. O sistema de combate foi um dos elementos que ajudaram a transformar Ocarina of Time em uma referência para os jogos de ação em terceira pessoa. No Nintendo 64, a introdução do Z-Targeting permitia que o jogador mantivesse a câmera focada em inimigos e personagens durante os confrontos, facilitando a movimentação em ambientes tridimensionais. Na versão de 2026, o combate recebeu atualizações, apontadas pela crítica como parte das melhorias da experiência. Entretanto, o remake não abandona a estrutura original. A exploração, a resolução de quebra-cabeças e a progressão pela aventura continuam sendo elementos centrais. Essa abordagem também dividiu opiniões. Enquanto alguns veículos elogiaram a fidelidade ao clássico, outros consideraram que a Nintendo poderia ter introduzido novidades mais expressivas. Entre as ausências mencionadas nas análises está o modo Master Quest, conhecido por oferecer uma versão alternativa dos desafios e masmorras de Ocarina of Time . Uma das mudanças mais significativas para o público brasileiro não está nos gráficos ou nas mecânicas, mas no idioma. O remake de Ocarina of Time é o primeiro jogo da franquia a receber localização completa em português brasileiro, incluindo textos e dublagem. Em entrevista exclusiva ao Omelete, Eiji Aonuma, produtor da série, explicou que o processo de localização mudou consideravelmente desde 1998. Naquela época, segundo ele, era comum que as traduções começassem apenas depois da conclusão do desenvolvimento, ou até mesmo após o lançamento original. Atualmente, a localização pode começar nas primeiras etapas de produção, permitindo que diferentes idiomas sejam incorporados ao projeto antes de sua finalização. Aonuma também destacou a importância de os jogadores brasileiros poderem acompanhar a aventura em seu próprio idioma. A novidade representa uma mudança importante na relação da Nintendo com o público brasileiro, especialmente considerando a longa espera por traduções oficiais da franquia. Apesar dos avanços tecnológicos, o remake não conseguiu superar a avaliação histórica do jogo original. A versão de Nintendo 64 mantém 99 pontos no Metacritic , a maior nota registrada na plataforma para um videogame. Já o remake de 2026 estreou com 96 pontos, considerando 81 análises da imprensa especializada, segundo levantamento divulgado pelo Critical Hits. Entre os veículos que atribuíram nota máxima à nova versão estão IGN, IGN Brasil, Eurogamer, GamesRadar+, VGC e Destructoid. As avaliações positivas destacaram principalmente a atualização visual, a apresentação cinematográfica e a preservação dos elementos que fizeram do original um clássico. Por outro lado, algumas análises apontaram que a abordagem conservadora limitou as novidades em relação à experiência de 1998. A comparação também exige considerar o contexto histórico: o Metascore original de Ocarina of Time é baseado em 22 avaliações, enquanto a versão de 2026 já reunia 81 análises em sua estreia. O Ocarina of Time de 1998 continua sendo uma referência histórica por sua contribuição ao desenvolvimento dos jogos tridimensionais. Seu sistema de combate, a estrutura das masmorras, a exploração de Hyrule e a maneira como integrou narrativa e jogabilidade influenciaram diferentes gerações de desenvolvedores. Já o remake de 2026 oferece uma maneira mais acessível de conhecer essa aventura, com apresentação modernizada e localização completa para o público brasileiro. A nova versão também demonstra que modernizar um clássico não significa necessariamente reinventá-lo. Enquanto o original permanece como um retrato de um momento decisivo da história dos videogames, o remake procura preservar essa experiência para uma nova geração. Depois de 28 anos, Ocarina of Time continua sendo o mesmo marco da franquia Zelda, mas agora pode ser descoberto de uma maneira muito diferente daquela apresentada aos jogadores do Nintendo 64. sources.title: Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director was "circling" a revival of BioWare's KOTOR for years
sources.text: "What if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games?" I imagine most BioWare fans would argue that the studio's peak happened somewhere between Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect 2. For me, though, the absolute high point was Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and I was always a little bitter that the devs moved on to create Mass Effect rather than finishing Revan's story in a proper KOTOR 3. That's why seeing Casey Hudson, original director of KOTOR, return with a spiritual successor in Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic is so exciting, and it's apparently been a long time coming. "It is really a dream project for us," Hudson says in an interview with The Fourth Curtain podcast . After leaving BioWare – for a second time – in 2020, he founded a new studio called Humanoid Origin, which was developing a "sci-fi action RPG" that would've been a "brand-new IP." That studio shuttered in 2024 after an "unexpected shortfall of funding," leaving Hudson to figure out what to do next. "We had lots of ideas, including, like, 'Do we get funding to continue with what we were doing? Are there other paths forward?' But over the years – myself and folks from our team, we worked on the original Knights of the Old Republic way back in the day, and since then BioWare also had the Old Republic MMO. So we've kept up connections with folks at Lucasfilm ," he says. Some time after Humanoid Origin shut down, Hudson explains, "the head of Disney Games reached out and said, 'Hey, what if we put a dent in the universe and made, essentially, the next in the line of Knights of the Old Republic games? The spiritual successor.'" Hudson says he'd been "circling" the idea of returning to KOTOR for some time. "It's something that I would love to do, but I was either doing other things or other projects. There were times when maybe it wasn't right for Lucasfilm, or they weren't ready for it. There wasn't really a fit." He was excited both by the possibility of returning to KOTOR and bringing back "some of the the top folks we've worked with," but surviving a studio shutdown leads you to "become the most skeptical person on earth," he says. "You don't really trust anyone to follow through with a deal or funding until things are signed, done, and legit." Getting those contracts finalized is how Hudson spent "the first half" of 2025. Then he spent the rest of the year "just starting to assemble our team, doing a prototype, and then creating the announcement trailer." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Yes, that means that Fate of the Old Republic had only barely entered development at the time of its reveal at The Game Awards last year, but Hudson seems confident we won't be waiting forever for it to be finished. The team works "at a very brisk pace," and he says we should expect "new announcements" sometime next year. Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic could be going for "a more simple hero's journey" to avoid BioWare's "self-indulgent" storytelling, says ex-Dragon Age boss Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. Rockstar Games’ long-awaited sequel is set to become the biggest launch in video game history, with millions of players expected to jump in during its opening days. Needless to say, the hype is very real, and the wait is almost over. But what if you don’t want to wait for your local release time? If you’re hoping to get into GTA 6 as early as possible on PlayStation 5, you’ll want to know about the so-called ‘New Zealand trick’. In this guide, I’ll walk you through exactly how it works and explain each step you need to follow to try and access the game at the earliest possible opportunity. Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming out on November 19, unlocking at midnight local time around the world. That means that some territories will be able to access the game ‘earlier’ than others, thanks to how time zones work. New Zealand is always the first territory to access new games because of where it’s situated on the planet. Isn’t that lovely for them? But you can use a (relatively) easy trick to play GTA 6 early on PS5 by using this New Zealand method to unlock the game 12 or 13 hours earlier than usual. The problem is that PlayStation makes the trick a bit of a hassle, since you have to jump through a few hoops to get GTA 6 early on PS5. It’s not as easy as it is to do the New Zealand trick on XBOX , where you just need to flip a switch in the console’s settings menu. When you come to the second step after making a New Zealand-based PSN account, you’ll want to head to your console settings, then to Users and Accounts, then Other, then Console Sharing and Offline Play, and flick that over to ‘enable’. When GTA comes out, you’ll be able to jump back to your main PlayStation 5 profile, and because you’ve enabled local sharing, you’ll be able to access the game early via your own account.
